description: Cross-implementation vectors for the alcove-signing-cert/v1 certificate and alcove-signing-identity/v1 identity file: ECDSA over P-256 with SHA-256, the public key an RFC 7518 EC JWK, the signature the fixed-length raw r||s (IEEE P1363). Each vector fixes a private key and an identity. The public coordinates and the certificate fingerprint are known answers -- the fingerprint covers the body and never the signature, so it stays deterministic though ECDSA signing is not. The self-signature is NOT a known answer and is verify-only: it was produced by the openssl CLI (see externalAnchors), so a suite that parses these certificates accepts a signature made outside this codebase. Regenerate with generate-signing-cert-vectors.mjs.

construction.signedBytes: canonicalBytes({ domain: signatureDomain, certificate: { version, algorithm, identity, publicKey: { kty, crv, x, y } } }) (RFC 8785)
construction.fingerprint: base64url(SHA-256(canonicalBytes({ domain: fingerprintDomain, certificate: <the same body> })))
construction.signatureEncoding: 64 bytes, r || s, each field element left-padded to 32 bytes. Not DER: a field of any other length is rejected rather than decoded.
construction.publicKeyEncoding: x and y are each exactly 32 bytes in canonical unpadded base64url. A coordinate carrying a leading zero byte, or written with base64 padding, is rejected rather than normalized.

vectors.name: p256-identity-a
vectors.description: A signing identity on the fixed private scalar 0x01..0x20, bound to a multi-line free-text identity. Any implementation given this private key must derive the same public coordinates and the same fingerprint, and must accept the checked-in certificate.

vectors.name: p256-identity-b
vectors.description: A second identity on the fixed private scalar 0xff..0xe0 with a different identity string, used as the mismatched-identity and non-matching-fingerprint counterpart to identity-a.
vectors.identity: Bureau of B, Office of Linkage

certificate.identity: Bureau of B, Office of Linkage
Bureau of B, Office of Linkage

externalAnchors.note: Every checked-in self-signature was produced by the openssl CLI named above (openssl dgst -sha256 -sign, DER read back through openssl asn1parse and re-encoded as the fixed-length raw r||s), over signed bytes this generator assembles from docs/spec/PROTOCOL.md. A suite that parses these certificates is therefore accepting a signature produced outside this codebase.
